items.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: a group had to come together and play some of the straight ahead stuff made popular by some of the great groups like Horace Silver, Art Blakey

ctx.x: The format was originally and still is, at that time jazz was getting very, very avant garde in Japan and very out. And there was a feeling by some people that a group had to come together and play some of the straight ahead stuff made popular by some of the great groups like Horace Silver, Art Blakey, da- da- da- da- da, in a little bit of a different way. And so we did an album and it was, outside of Blood, Sweat & Tears, I have never been involved in a band that had that kind of reaction to it. Never. I mean…

Tears of course was in a class by itself. You know how big that band was at the time. That was a real trip. We were the second biggest band in the world to the Beatles. But this band was very far removed from that kind of success, but way more successful than anything else I was with outside of BS&T. And this one was called MJQ. They call it MJQ. So maybe if I change my name from Lew Soloff’s Food Group to LSFD maybe something will happen. Yeah, maybe some initials, maybe that’ll do it. Anyway just to let you…
